[App menu] Menu item: About YourAppName · Action: Displays the About window for your app, which includes copyright and version information. · Guidance: Prefer a short name of 16 characters or fewer. Don’t include a version number.

[App menu] Menu item: Settings… · Action: Opens your settings settings window, or your app’s page in iPadOS Settings. · Guidance: Use only for app-level settings. If you also offer document-specific settings, put them in the File menu.

[App menu] Menu item: Optional app-specific items · Action: Performs custom app-level setting or configuration actions. · Guidance: List custom app-configuration items after the Settings item and within the same group.
[App menu] Menu item: Services (macOS only) · Action: Displays a submenu of services from the system and other apps that apply to the current context.

[App menu] Menu item: Hide YourAppName (macOS only) · Action: Hides your app and all of its windows, and then activates the most recently used app. · Guidance: Use the same short app name you supply for the About item.
[App menu] Menu item: Hide Others (macOS only) · Action: Hides all other open apps and their windows.
[App menu] Menu item: Show All (macOS only) · Action: Shows all other open apps and their windows behind your app’s windows.

[App menu] Menu item: Quit YourAppName · Action: Quits your app. Pressing Option changes Quit YourAppName to Quit and Keep Windows. · Guidance: Use the same short app name you supply for the About item.

[File menu] Menu item: New Item · Action: Creates a new document, file, or window. · Guidance: For Item , use a term that names the type of item your app creates. For example, Calendar uses Event and Calendar .

[File menu] Menu item: Open · Action: Can open the selected item or present an interface in which people select an item to open. · Guidance: If people need to select an item in a separate interface, an ellipsis follows the command to indicate that more input is required.

[File menu] Menu item: Open Recent · Action: Displays a submenu that lists recently opened documents and files that people can select, and typically includes a Clear Menu item. · Guidance: List document and filenames that people recognize in the submenu; don’t display file paths. List the documents in the order people last opened them, with the most recently opened document first.

[File menu] Menu item: Close · Action: Closes the current window or document. Pressing Option changes Close to Close All. For a tab-based window, Close Tab replaces Close. · Guidance: In a tab-based window, consider adding a Close Window item to let people close the entire window with one click or tap.
[File menu] Menu item: Close Tab · Action: Closes the current tab in a tab-based window. Pressing Option changes Close Tab to Close Other Tabs.

[File menu] Menu item: Close File · Action: Closes the current file and all its associated windows. · Guidance: Consider supporting this menu item if your app can open multiple views of the same file.

[File menu] Menu item: Save · Action: Saves the current document or file. · Guidance: Automatically save changes periodically as people work so they don’t need to keep choosing File > Save. For a new document, prompt people for a name and location. If you need to let people save a file in multiple formats, prefer a pop-up menu that lets people choose a format in the Save sheet.
[File menu] Menu item: Save All · Action: Saves all open documents.

[File menu] Menu item: Duplicate · Action: Duplicates the current document, leaving both documents open. Pressing Option changes Duplicate to Save As. · Guidance: Prefer Duplicate to menu items like Save As, Export, Copy To, and Save To because these items don’t clarify the relationship between the original file and the new one.
[File menu] Menu item: Rename… · Action: Lets people change the name of the current document.
[File menu] Menu item: Move To… · Action: Prompts people to choose a new location for the document.

[File menu] Menu item: Export As… · Action: Prompts people for a name, output location, and export file format. After exporting the file, the current document remains open; the exported file doesn’t open. · Guidance: Reserve the Export As item for when you need to let people export content in a format your app doesn’t typically handle.

[File menu] Menu item: Revert To · Action: When people turn on autosaving, displays a submenu that lists recent document versions and an option to display the version browser. After people choose a version to restore, it replaces the current document.

[File menu] Menu item: Page Setup… · Action: Opens a panel for specifying printing parameters like paper size and printing orientation. A document can save the printing parameters that people specify. · Guidance: Include the Page Setup item if you need to support printing parameters that apply to a specific document. Parameters that are global in nature, like a printer’s name, or that people change frequently, like the number of copies to print, belong in the Print panel.
[File menu] Menu item: Print… · Action: Opens the standard Print panel, which lets people print to a printer, send a fax, or save as a PDF.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Undo · Action: Reverses the effect of the previous user operation. · Guidance: Clarify the target of the undo. For example, if people just selected a menu item, you can append the item’s title, such as Undo Paste and Match Style. For a text entry operation, you might append the word Typing to give Undo Typing.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Redo · Action: Reverses the effect of the previous Undo operation. · Guidance: Clarify the target of the redo. For example, if people just reversed a menu item selection, you can append the item’s title, such as Redo Paste and Match Style. For a text entry operation, you might append the word Typing to give Redo Typing.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Cut · Action: Removes the selected data and stores it on the Clipboard, replacing the previous contents of the Clipboard.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Copy · Action: Duplicates the selected data and stores it on the Clipboard.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Paste · Action: Inserts the contents of the Clipboard at the current insertion point. The Clipboard contents remain unchanged, permitting people to choose Paste multiple times.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Paste and Match Style · Action: Inserts the contents of the Clipboard at the current insertion point, matching the style of the inserted text to the surrounding text.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Delete · Action: Removes the selected data, but doesn’t place it on the Clipboard. · Guidance: Provide a Delete menu item instead of an Erase or Clear menu item. Choosing Delete is the equivalent of pressing the Delete key, so it’s important for the naming to be consistent.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Select All · Action: Highlights all selectable content in the current document or text container.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Find · Action: Displays a submenu containing menu items for performing search operations in the current document or text container. Standard submenus include: Find, Find and Replace, Find Next, Find Previous, Use Selection for Find, and Jump to Selection.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Spelling and Grammar · Action: Displays a submenu containing menu items for checking for and correcting spelling and grammar in the current document or text container. Standard submenus include: Show Spelling and Grammar, Check Document Now, Check Spelling While Typing, Check Grammar With Spelling, and Correct Spelling Automatically.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Substitutions · Action: Displays a submenu containing items that let people toggle automatic substitutions while they type in a document or text container. Standard submenus include: Show Substitutions, Smart Copy/Paste, Smart Quotes, Smart Dashes, Smart Links, Data Detectors, and Text Replacement.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Transformations · Action: Displays a submenu containing items that transform selected text. Standard submenus include: Make Uppercase, Make Lowercase, and Capitalize.
[Edit menu] Menu item: Speech · Action: Displays a submenu containing Start Speaking and Stop Speaking items, which control when the system audibly reads selected text.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Start Dictation · Action: Opens the dictation window and converts spoken words into text that’s added at the current insertion point. The system automatically adds the Start Dictation menu item at the bottom of the Edit menu.

[Edit menu] Menu item: Emoji & Symbols · Action: Displays a Character Viewer, which includes emoji, symbols, and other characters people can insert at the current insertion point. The system automatically adds the Emoji & Symbols menu item at the bottom of the Edit menu.

[Format menu] Menu item: Font · Action: Displays a submenu containing items for adjusting font attributes of the selected text. Standard submenus include: Show Fonts, Bold, Italic, Underline, Bigger, Smaller, Show Colors, Copy Style, and Paste Style.

[Format menu] Menu item: Text · Action: Displays a submenu containing items for adjusting text attributes of the selected text. Standard submenus include: Align Left, Align Center, Justify, Align Right, Writing Direction, Show Ruler, Copy Ruler, and Paste Ruler.
[View menu] Menu item: Show/Hide Tab Bar · Action: Toggles the visibility of the tab-bars tab bar above the body area in a tab-based window
[View menu] Menu item: Show All Tabs/Exit Tab Overview · Action: Enters and exits a view (similar to Mission Control) that provides an overview of all open tabs in a tab-based window
[View menu] Menu item: Show/Hide Toolbar · Action: In a window that includes a toolbars toolbar , toggles the toolbar’s visibility
[View menu] Menu item: Customize Toolbar · Action: In a window that includes a toolbar, opens a view that lets people customize toolbar items
[View menu] Menu item: Show/Hide Sidebar · Action: In a window that includes a sidebars sidebar , toggles the sidebar’s visibility
[View menu] Menu item: Enter/Exit Full Screen · Action: In an app that supports a going-full-screen full-screen experience , opens the window at full-screen size in a new space
[Window menu] Menu item: Minimize · Action: Minimizes the active window to the Dock. Pressing the Option key changes this item to Minimize All.

[Window menu] Menu item: Zoom · Action: Toggles between a predefined size appropriate to the window’s content and the window size people set. Pressing the Option key changes this item to Zoom All. · Guidance: Avoid using Zoom to enter or exit full-screen mode. The the-menu-bar#View-menu supports these functions.
[Window menu] Menu item: Show Previous Tab · Action: Shows the tab before the current tab in a tab-based window.
[Window menu] Menu item: Show Next Tab · Action: Shows the tab after the current tab in a tab-based window.
[Window menu] Menu item: Move Tab to New Window · Action: Opens the current tab in a new window.
[Window menu] Menu item: Merge All Windows · Action: Combines all open windows into a single tabbed window.

[Window menu] Menu item: Enter/Exit Full Screen · Action: In an app that supports a going-full-screen full-screen experience , opens the window at full-screen size in a new space. · Guidance: Include this item in the Window menu only if your app doesn’t have a View menu. In this scenario, continue to provide separate Minimize and Zoom menu items.

[Window menu] Menu item: Bring All to Front · Action: Brings all an app’s open windows to the front, maintaining their onscreen location, size, and layering order. (Clicking the app icon in the Dock has the same effect.) Pressing the Option key changes this item to Arrange in Front, which brings an app’s windows to the front in a neatly tiled arrangement.

[Window menu] Menu item: Name of an open app-specific window · Action: Brings the selected window to the front. · Guidance: List the currently open windows in alphabetical order for easy scanning. Avoid listing panels or other modal views.
[Help menu] Menu item: Send YourAppName Feedback to Apple · Action: Opens the Feedback Assistant, in which people can provide feedback.
[Help menu] Menu item: YourAppName Help · Action: When the content uses the Help Book format, opens the content in the built-in Help Viewer.

[Help menu] Menu item: Additional Item · Guidance: Use a separator between your primary help documentation and additional items, which might include registration information or release notes. Keep the total the number of items you list in the Help menu small to avoid overwhelming people with too many choices when they need help. Alternatively, consider linking to additional items from within your help documentation.

[Best practices] Category: Solo ambient · Meaning: Sound isn’t essential, but it silences other audio. For example, a game with a soundtrack. · Behavior: Responds to the silence switch. Doesn’t mix with other sounds. Doesn’t play in the background.

[Best practices] Category: Ambient · Meaning: Sound isn’t essential, and it doesn’t silence other audio. For example, a game that lets people play music from another app during gameplay in place of the game’s soundtrack. · Behavior: Responds to the silence switch. Mixes with other sounds. Doesn’t play in the background.

[Best practices] Category: Playback · Meaning: Sound is essential and might mix with other audio. For example, an audiobook or educational app that teaches a foreign language, which people might want to listen to after leaving the app. · Behavior: Doesn’t respond to the silence switch. May or may not mix with other sounds. Can play in the background.

[Best practices] Category: Record · Meaning: Sound is recorded. For example, a note-taking app that offers an audio recording mode. An app of this nature might switch its category to playback if it lets people play the recorded notes. · Behavior: Doesn’t respond to the silence switch. Doesn’t mix with other sounds. Can record in the background.

[Best practices] Category: Play and record · Meaning: Sound is recorded and played, potentially simultaneously. For example, an audio messaging or video calling app. · Behavior: Doesn’t respond to the silence switch. May or may not mix with other sounds. Can record and play in the background.
